pinyin: wén wǔ zhī dào, yī zhāng yī chí
literal: King Wen and King Wu's · way · one · tighten · one · loosen
natural: the way of the sage kings: tighten, then loosen

meaning.en: The way of the sage kings was to alternate tension with relaxation; effort and rest must be balanced.
meaning.zh: 周文王、周武王治国之道，就是松紧结合、张弛有度；比喻工作与休息要劳逸结合。

equivalents: all work and no play is no way to rule
keep a balance between effort and rest

examples.zh: 文武之道，一张一弛，连续加班并不是长久之计。
examples.en: The way is to tighten and loosen in turn; endless overtime is no long-term plan.

examples.zh: 备考也要文武之道，一张一弛，别把弦绷得太紧。
examples.en: Even exam prep should alternate tension and ease; don't pull the string too tight.

examples.zh: 教练说文武之道，一张一弛，今天全队休息一天。
examples.en: The coach said that a good regime tightens and loosens in turn, so the whole squad rests today.

story.en: Confucius told Zigong that a bow kept always taut or always slack would not serve: 'Taut without slack, even Kings Wen and Wu could not manage; slack without taut, they would not do; one taut, one slack, that is the way of Wen and Wu' (一张一弛，文武之道也).
story.zh: 孔子对子贡说：“张而不弛，文武弗能也；弛而不张，文武弗为也；一张一弛，文武之道也。”

usage.en: Quoted as a principle in management, study and training. Often shortened to 一张一弛. Formal.
usage.zh: 常在管理、学习、训练中作为原则引用，也常缩略为“一张一弛”。较正式。

natural: its destined span has run out

meaning.en: Its allotted fortune has run out; a regime, business or person is doomed to collapse.
meaning.zh: 指命中注定的运数已经终结，政权、事业或人已走到尽头，不可挽回。

examples.zh: 这家老字号经营不善，大家都说它气数已尽。
examples.en: The old brand was badly run, and everyone said its days were numbered.

examples.zh: 王朝气数已尽，再强的将领也挽不回败局。
examples.en: The dynasty's fortune was spent, and not even the best general could reverse the defeat.

examples.zh: 他觉得自己气数已尽，索性什么也不争了。
examples.en: Feeling his luck had run out, he simply stopped fighting for anything.

usage.en: Usually predicate or a quoted judgement; sounds fatalistic. Used of regimes, firms and sometimes people.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或引用的判断，带宿命色彩；用于政权、企业，有时也指人。

natural: repair bridges and mend roads

meaning.en: To do public good by building bridges and repairing roads; a traditional picture of charity.
meaning.zh: 修建桥梁、修补道路，泛指为乡里做公益善事。

equivalents: build bridges and roads for the community

examples.zh: 老人一生修桥补路，乡亲们都敬重他。
examples.en: The old man spent his life building bridges and mending roads, and the villagers respected him.

examples.zh: 他发家后回乡修桥补路，回报家乡。
examples.en: After getting rich he returned home to repair roads and bridges for his hometown.

examples.zh: 修桥补路积德行善，是这里的老传统。
examples.en: Mending bridges and roads as a good deed is an old tradition here.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; praises quiet public-spirited charity, often paired with 积德行善.
usage.zh: 作谓语、定语，称赞默默做公益的善举，常与“积德行善”连用。

natural: this trend must not grow

meaning.en: A warning that a bad practice must be stopped now, before it spreads.
meaning.zh: 指不良风气不能任其发展，应当及时制止。

equivalents: this must not become a trend

examples.zh: 考试作弊的事屡有发生，此风不可长。
examples.en: Cheating in exams keeps happening; this must not become a trend.

examples.zh: 请客送礼，此风不可长，必须严肃处理。
examples.en: Wining, dining and gift-giving must not become the norm and will be dealt with strictly.

examples.zh: 有人插队，大家都说此风不可长。
examples.en: Someone jumped the queue, and everyone said it must not be tolerated.

usage.en: Stand-alone remark in speeches, editorials and everyday criticism. 长 is zhǎng (grow), not cháng.
usage.zh: 常作独立评语，用于讲话、评论和日常批评。“长”读 zhǎng。

natural: a blind man on a blind horse

meaning.en: Blindly pressing ahead without direction or knowledge, heading straight for disaster.
meaning.zh: 比喻毫无方向、盲目行事，十分危险。

examples.zh: 没有调研就盲目扩张，简直是盲人骑瞎马。
examples.en: Expanding without any research is like a blind man riding a blind horse.

examples.zh: 新手不看地图就闯进山里，真是盲人骑瞎马。
examples.en: The novices went into the mountains without a map, courting disaster.

examples.zh: 对市场一无所知就投钱，无异于盲人骑瞎马。
examples.en: To invest money while knowing nothing of the market is to ride blind.

usage.en: Usually said as a criticism or warning; often continued as 夜半临深池 ('at midnight, beside a deep pool').
usage.zh: 多作批评或警告；常接下句“夜半临深池”。

pinyin: hēi yún yā chéng chéng yù cuī
literal: black · clouds · press · city · city · about to · collapse
natural: black clouds press on the city until it seems to crumble

meaning.en: Dark clouds bear down on the city as if to crush its walls; a vivid image of a crushing threat or crisis.
meaning.zh: 乌云沉沉压向城头，仿佛要把城墙压垮；比喻敌军压境或形势危急、压力巨大。

equivalents: black clouds massing over the city

examples.zh: 乌云翻滚，真有黑云压城城欲摧的气势。
examples.en: The clouds rolled in with the force of 'black clouds pressing the city to ruin'.

examples.zh: 对手兵临城下，球队面临黑云压城城欲摧的局面。
examples.en: With the rival at the gates, the team faced a crisis as if black clouds were crushing the city.

examples.zh: 诗人用黑云压城城欲摧写出战前的紧张。
examples.en: The poet uses 'black clouds press the city' to capture the tension before battle.

story.en: Li He's frontier poem opens with the besieged city: 'Black clouds press on the city, the city seems about to crumble; armour glints in the sun like golden scales' (黑云压城城欲摧，甲光向日金鳞开).
story.zh: 李贺《雁门太守行》开篇：“黑云压城城欲摧，甲光向日金鳞开。”写边城被围的紧张气氛。

usage.en: Quoted for ominous weather or for an overwhelming threat. Often paired with the next line 甲光向日金鳞开. Literary.
usage.zh: 用于描写阴云密布或压力沉重的形势，常与下句“甲光向日金鳞开”连用。书面语。

natural: kill without a drop of blood showing

meaning.en: To ruin someone by cunning and covert means, leaving no obvious trace of violence.
meaning.zh: 比喻用阴险、隐蔽的手段害人，表面上看不出痕迹。

examples.zh: 他表面客气，实际上是杀人不见血的高手。
examples.en: He is all politeness, but a master of ruining people without a trace.

examples.zh: 职场里有人靠造谣杀人不见血。
examples.en: In some workplaces people use rumours to destroy colleagues without ever raising a hand.

examples.zh: 这种杀人不见血的手段，比公开对抗更可怕。
examples.en: Such bloodless methods are scarier than open confrontation.

usage.en: Describes people or tactics; critical. Often continues 杀人不见血的刀 'a knife that draws no blood'.
usage.zh: 形容人或手段，含贬义；常说“杀人不见血的刀”。

natural: deep worry opens the way to wisdom

meaning.en: Great hardship and anxiety awaken able leaders and spur a state or person to greatness.
meaning.zh: 深重的忧患会激发圣明，使国家或个人在困境中奋起。

examples.zh: 殷忧启圣，多难兴邦，这个民族正是在苦难中崛起的。
examples.en: Deep hardship breeds sages and trials strengthen a nation; this people rose out of suffering.

examples.zh: 公司几乎破产，反而殷忧启圣，逼出了新产品。
examples.en: The firm nearly went bankrupt, and that trouble spurred it to a new product.

examples.zh: 他把失败看作殷忧启圣的机会。
examples.en: He treats failure as a chance for hardship to open the way to wisdom.

usage.en: Literary and formal; usually paired with 多难兴邦. 殷 here means 'deep', pronounced yīn.
usage.zh: 书面语、较正式，常与“多难兴邦”连用。“殷”在这里是“深”，读 yīn。

natural: the pick of the day

meaning.en: Among the best people of one's age or a given moment; a top choice at the time.
meaning.zh: 指当时最出色的人物或事物。

equivalents: among the best of their time

examples.zh: 这支队伍人才济济，堪称一时之选。
examples.en: The team is full of talent, truly the best of its day.

examples.zh: 评委都是业内一时之选。
examples.en: The judges are among the leading figures of the field.

examples.zh: 他在那个年代是一时之选的编剧。
examples.en: In that era he was among the finest screenwriters.

usage.en: Praise for people or groups; formal. Predicate or attributive ('一时之选的……').
usage.zh: 用于称赞人物或群体，较正式，作谓语或定语。

pinyin: tài shān yā dǐng bù wān yāo
literal: Mount Tai · press · top · not · bend · waist
natural: not stooping though Mount Tai presses down

meaning.en: Standing firm and unbowed even under overwhelming pressure.
meaning.zh: 形容在巨大压力面前依然挺立不屈，毫不畏惧。

equivalents: stand firm against the heaviest pressure

examples.zh: 面对巨额债务，他泰山压顶不弯腰，一步步还清了。
examples.en: Facing a huge debt he stood unbowed and paid it off step by step.

examples.zh: 革命者泰山压顶不弯腰，从不向困难低头。
examples.en: Revolutionaries stand firm though Mount Tai presses down, and never bow to hardship.

examples.zh: 泰山压顶不弯腰，这是她面对逆境的态度。
examples.en: Unbent though Mount Tai crushes down: that is her attitude to adversity.

usage.en: Slogan-like, heroic in tone; often paired with 面不改色心不跳. Predicate or quoted motto.
usage.zh: 带口号色彩，语气豪迈，常与“面不改色心不跳”连用。作谓语或座右铭。

natural: face danger and give one's life

meaning.en: To be ready to lay down one's life when the nation or a just cause is in peril.
meaning.zh: 面对危难时勇于献出生命。

equivalents: lay down one's life in a crisis

examples.zh: 他临危授命，毫不犹豫地冲进火场。
examples.en: Facing danger he risked his life without hesitation and rushed into the fire.

examples.zh: 国家有难，志士临危授命。
examples.en: When the nation is in peril, patriots give their lives.

examples.zh: 先烈们临危授命的精神值得我们铭记。
examples.en: We should remember the spirit of the martyrs who gave their lives in danger.

story.en: Zilu asked what makes a complete person, and Confucius's answer includes: 'seeing danger, give up his life' (见危授命), together with thinking of righteousness at the sight of profit.
story.zh: 《论语·宪问》子路问成人，孔子答中有“见利思义，见危授命，久要不忘平生之言，亦可以为成人矣”。

usage.en: 授命 means 'surrender one's life'. Do not confuse with the modern 临危受命 (take up a post in a crisis), a common mix-up. Formal.
usage.zh: “授命”指献出生命。注意与现代常说的“临危受命”（危难时接受任命）区别，二者常被混用。较正式。

pinyin: miàn bù gǎi sè xīn bù tiào
literal: face · not · change · colour · heart · not · jump
natural: the face doesn't change colour, the heart doesn't race

meaning.en: To stay completely calm in a frightening or embarrassing situation; sometimes used of shameless lying.
meaning.zh: 遇到危险或尴尬场面时十分镇定，毫无惧色；有时也指说谎不脸红。

examples.zh: 他面对劫匪，面不改色心不跳。
examples.en: He faced the robber without turning a hair.

examples.zh: 她撒起谎来面不改色心不跳。
examples.en: She lies without so much as a blush.

examples.zh: 过山车上，他居然面不改色心不跳。
examples.en: On the roller coaster he stayed perfectly calm.

usage.en: Colloquial; praise for coolness, or ironic when used of lying. Predicate or adverbial.
usage.zh: 口语，可赞其镇定，也可反讽撒谎面不改色。作谓语或状语。

pinyin: yǐ qí hūn hūn, shǐ rén zhāo zhāo
literal: with · one's own · murkiness · make · people · clear
natural: using one's own confusion to enlighten others

meaning.en: You cannot make others understand what you do not understand yourself.
meaning.zh: 自己都糊涂，却想让别人明白；比喻自己不懂就无法教人。

equivalents: the blind cannot lead the blind
you can't teach what you don't know

examples.zh: 自己都没弄懂，怎么讲给学生？以其昏昏，使人昭昭是行不通的。
examples.en: You cannot teach what you have not grasped; trying to enlighten others from your own confusion never works.

examples.zh: 老师备课不充分，只能以其昏昏，使人昭昭。
examples.en: A teacher who has not prepared can only try to enlighten others from their own muddle.

examples.zh: 写科普文章要先吃透，免得以其昏昏，使人昭昭。
examples.en: Before writing popular science, understand it fully, lest you try to clarify things for others while confused yourself.

story.en: Mencius said: 'In the past, worthy men used their own clarity to make others clear; today people use their own murkiness to try to make others clear' (贤者以其昭昭，使人昭昭；今以其昏昏，使人昭昭).
story.zh: 孟子曰：“贤者以其昭昭，使人昭昭；今以其昏昏，使人昭昭。”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 约前4世纪

usage.en: Usually used as a warning to teachers, writers and speakers. Literary; often quoted with its positive counterpart 以其昭昭，使人昭昭.
usage.zh: 多用来告诫教师、作者、讲者。书面语；常与正面的“以其昭昭，使人昭昭”对举。

text: 一朝权在手，便把令来行
pinyin: yī zhāo quán zài shǒu, biàn bǎ lìng lái xíng
literal: one · morning · power · in · hand · then · take · orders · carry out
natural: once power is in hand, start giving orders

meaning.en: Said of those who start throwing their weight around the moment they gain authority.
meaning.zh: 形容人一旦掌握权力，就立刻发号施令、作威作福。

equivalents: a little authority and they start barking orders

examples.zh: 他刚当上组长，就像一朝权在手，便把令来行。
examples.en: He had just become team leader and was already throwing his weight around.

examples.zh: 小人得志，往往一朝权在手，便把令来行。
examples.en: Petty people who rise often start issuing orders the moment they have power.

examples.zh: 别以为一朝权在手，便把令来行就能服众。
examples.en: Don't think that giving orders as soon as you have power will win people over.

usage.en: Mocking; chiefly of newly promoted people. 朝 here is zhāo (morning/one day), as in 一朝一夕.
usage.zh: 带讽刺意味，多指新得权势者。“朝”读 zhāo。

natural: an orchid in an empty valley

meaning.en: A quietly fragrant orchid in a deserted valley; a person of refined character who lives apart from the crowd.
meaning.zh: 空旷山谷中幽香淡雅的兰花；比喻品格高洁、不求闻达的人。

equivalents: an orchid in a hidden valley

examples.zh: 她气质如空谷幽兰，不争不抢。
examples.en: Her presence is like an orchid in a quiet valley, neither pushy nor showy.

examples.zh: 这位隐居的学者宛如空谷幽兰。
examples.en: The reclusive scholar is like an orchid in an empty glen.

examples.zh: 那首曲子清雅悠远，像空谷幽兰。
examples.en: The piece is graceful and distant, like an orchid in a hidden valley.

usage.en: Praise, mostly for women or reclusive gentlemen; also a metaphor for refined music or art. Literary.
usage.zh: 多用来赞美女子或隐士的高雅品格，也比喻清雅的音乐、艺术。书面语。

natural: understand things and get affairs done

meaning.en: To grasp the nature of things and use that knowledge to accomplish practical tasks.
meaning.zh: 揭示事物的规律，并据此成就事业、办成事情。

equivalents: understand the world and get things done

examples.zh: 科学家的使命就是开物成务，造福社会。
examples.en: The scientist's mission is to understand things and put that knowledge to work for society.

examples.zh: 这所学院强调开物成务，注重学以致用。
examples.en: The college stresses learning that gets things done and emphasises practical application.

examples.zh: 他一生开物成务，留下许多发明。
examples.en: All his life he turned understanding into achievement, leaving many inventions.

story.en: The Commentary on the Appendices says the Changes 'open up things and complete tasks, and cover the ways of the world' (夫《易》开物成务，冒天下之道).
story.zh: 《周易·系辞上》：“夫《易》开物成务，冒天下之道，如斯而已者也。”

usage.en: Literary and formal; used in praise of practical knowledge, inventors and reformers. Often seen as a motto or book title.
usage.zh: 书面语、较正式，赞扬学以致用、发明和变革，也常作格言或书名。

literal: respect · the old · honour · the worthy
natural: respect the old and honour the worthy

meaning.en: To respect the elderly and honour people of talent and virtue.
meaning.zh: 尊敬老人，尊重有德有才的人。

examples.zh: 我们的社区一向敬老尊贤。
examples.en: Our community has always honoured elders and the worthy.

examples.zh: 学校倡导敬老尊贤的好风气。
examples.en: The school promotes a good culture of respecting the old and the worthy.

examples.zh: 敬老尊贤是传统美德。
examples.en: Respecting the old and honouring the worthy is a traditional virtue.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; common in speeches on traditional virtues. Formal.
usage.zh: 作谓语、定语，常见于谈传统美德的讲话。较正式。

pinyin: bù jīn xì xíng, zhōng lěi dà dé
literal: not · take care over · small · conduct · in the end · burden · great · virtue
natural: careless of small conduct, one finally spoils great virtue

meaning.en: If you are careless about small matters of conduct, you will in the end ruin your great character.
meaning.zh: 不注意小节，最终会损害大德；比喻小处不检点会毁掉大节。

equivalents: watch the little things or lose the big picture

examples.zh: 不矜细行，终累大德，干部更要从小事上严格要求自己。
examples.en: Careless small conduct finally damages great virtue, so officials must hold themselves strictly to account even in small matters.

examples.zh: 他因为几次小小的贪念栽了跟头，真是不矜细行，终累大德。
examples.en: A few petty acts of greed brought him down: carelessness in small things ruined his great reputation.

examples.zh: 家长常用不矜细行，终累大德教育孩子注意小节。
examples.en: Parents often use this saying to teach children to mind small details of behaviour.

story.en: In the 'Lü Ao' chapter the Duke of Shao warns King Wu: 'If you are not careful of small conduct, you will in the end burden your great virtue; in raising a hill of nine ren, one basket short spoils the work' (不矜细行，终累大德).
story.zh: 《尚书·旅獒》召公告诫武王：“不矜细行，终累大德。为山九仞，功亏一篑。”

date.zh: 东晋 · 4世纪初（今传古文《尚书》）
date.en: Eastern Jin, early 4th c. (Old Text Documents as transmitted)

usage.en: Moral warning, common in speeches on integrity and discipline. 累 here is lěi (burden, harm), 矜 means 'take care'. Formal.
usage.zh: 用于廉洁、修养方面的告诫。“累”读 lěi，意为损害；“矜”意为谨慎。较正式。

pinyin: tiān ruò yǒu qíng tiān yì lǎo
literal: Heaven · if · had · feeling · Heaven · too · would age
natural: if Heaven had feelings it too would grow old

meaning.en: If Heaven could feel, it too would age with grief; a cry of deep sorrow over parting and change.
meaning.zh: 如果上天也有感情，也会因悲伤而衰老；形容悲痛至极，常感叹离别与世事沧桑。

equivalents: even Heaven would grow old with grief
sorrow too deep for Heaven to bear

examples.zh: 看着亲人远去，他只想说天若有情天亦老。
examples.en: Watching his family leave, all he could say was that even Heaven would age with such grief.

examples.zh: 这首词读来让人感叹天若有情天亦老。
examples.en: Reading this lyric, one sighs that even Heaven would grow old at such sorrow.

examples.zh: 毛泽东化用“天若有情天亦老”，写下“人间正道是沧桑”。
examples.en: Mao Zedong borrowed 'if Heaven had feeling it would age' and answered it with 'the right path of the world is vicissitude'.

story.en: Li He's poem imagines the bronze immortal being carted away from the Han court: 'Withered orchids see the guest off on the Xianyang road; if Heaven had feeling, Heaven too would grow old' (衰兰送客咸阳道，天若有情天亦老).
story.zh: 李贺《金铜仙人辞汉歌》：“衰兰送客咸阳道，天若有情天亦老。”写铜人被迁离汉宫的悲怆。

usage.en: Quoted for grief at parting or the passing of time; often matched with the line 月如无恨月常圆. Literary.
usage.zh: 用于抒发离别之悲或感慨世事变迁，常与“月如无恨月常圆”对举。书面语。

natural: old in years, faded in looks

meaning.en: Growing old and losing one's youthful good looks, especially said of women.
meaning.zh: 年纪大了，容貌衰退，多指女子。

examples.zh: 她年老色衰后，被主人冷落了。
examples.en: When she grew old and lost her looks, her master neglected her.

examples.zh: 演员最怕年老色衰，戏路越走越窄。
examples.en: Actresses fear the day they age and fade, when their roles dwindle.

examples.zh: 不要因为年老色衰就看轻自己。
examples.en: Don't belittle yourself just because you are older and your looks have faded.

usage.en: Traditionally about women losing favour; today often critical of the attitude behind it. Predicate.
usage.zh: 传统上多指女子失宠；今天常带批评这种观念的意味。作谓语。

natural: dispel illness and lengthen life

meaning.en: To drive away illness and live longer; often a wish for health and long life.
meaning.zh: 消除疾病，延长寿命；常用作祝愿健康长寿。

equivalents: ward off illness and live long

examples.zh: 这套养生功法据说能祛病延年。
examples.en: This set of exercises is said to ward off illness and prolong life.

examples.zh: 祝老人家祛病延年，福寿安康。
examples.en: May you shake off illness, live long and be blessed with health.

examples.zh: 坚持散步，也有祛病延年的效果。
examples.en: Walking regularly can also help prevent illness and extend life.

usage.en: Used for health regimens and as a wish to the elderly. 祛 is qū. Formal.
usage.zh: 常用于养生功法或祝福老人。“祛”读 qū。较正式。

literal: not · as good as · return · go
natural: better to go home

meaning.en: Better go home; a homesick sigh, imitating the call of the cuckoo.
meaning.zh: 不如回家去吧；表达思乡之情，相传杜鹃鸣声似“不如归去”。

examples.zh: 在外漂泊多年，他常常想起不如归去。
examples.en: After years of drifting, he often thinks it would be better to go home.

examples.zh: 听见杜鹃声声“不如归去”，游子鼻子一酸。
examples.en: Hearing the cuckoo cry 'better go home', the wanderer felt a pang.

examples.zh: 工作不顺，她心里涌起不如归去的念头。
examples.en: Things went badly at work, and she began to think it better to go home.

usage.en: Lyrical; the cuckoo's call is heard as 'bù rú guī qù', a classic image of homesickness.
usage.zh: 带抒情色彩；古人把杜鹃叫声听作“不如归去”，是思乡的经典意象。

natural: the ends of the earth within a hand's reach

meaning.en: Even when far apart, hearts feel close; distance at the ends of the earth seems like a few steps.
meaning.zh: 相隔虽远，感觉却近在眼前；多形容挚友或亲人心灵相通，不因距离疏远。

equivalents: far apart yet near at heart

examples.zh: 有了视频通话，天涯咫尺，亲人如在眼前。
examples.en: With video calls, even the ends of the earth feel near and family seems right there.

examples.zh: 真正的知己，纵然天涯咫尺也不觉遥远。
examples.en: True friends feel close however far apart they are.

examples.zh: 科技让世界变得天涯咫尺。
examples.en: Technology makes distant places feel next door.

usage.en: Not the same as 咫尺天涯 (near but unreachable): 天涯咫尺 means far yet felt as near. Literary.
usage.zh: 与“咫尺天涯”（近在眼前却如远隔天涯）意思相反：“天涯咫尺”指远而如近。书面语。

natural: break it open and crumble it fine

meaning.en: To explain something in minute detail, breaking it down until anyone can follow.
meaning.zh: 把道理或事情讲得细致入微、一点一点分析清楚。

equivalents: break it down piece by piece

examples.zh: 老师把这道题掰开揉碎讲了一遍。
examples.en: The teacher broke the problem down piece by piece.

examples.zh: 我把利害关系掰开揉碎地跟他说了。
examples.en: I laid out the pros and cons for him in full detail.

examples.zh: 这本书把复杂概念掰开揉碎，通俗易懂。
examples.en: The book breaks complex concepts down, so they are easy to understand.

usage.en: Colloquial; usually 把……掰开揉碎 + verb. Praise for patient explanation, though it can hint at over-explaining.
usage.zh: 口语，常说“把……掰开揉碎地讲”。多赞耐心细致，有时也含啰嗦之意。

natural: be as careful at the end as at the start

meaning.en: To stay as careful at the end of a task as at the beginning, so it doesn't fail near the finish.
meaning.zh: 事情到最后仍像开头一样谨慎，才不会功亏一篑。

equivalents: finish as carefully as you begin
keep up the care to the very end

examples.zh: 项目越到收尾越要慎终如始。
examples.en: The closer a project is to completion, the more we must stay as careful as at the start.

examples.zh: 登山到最后一段，更要慎终如始。
examples.en: On the last stretch of a climb, stay as careful as at the start.

examples.zh: 他做事慎终如始，从不松懈。
examples.en: He is as careful at the end as at the beginning and never slackens.

story.en: Laozi says: 'People often fail on the brink of success; if you are as careful at the end as at the start, there will be no failure' (慎终如始，则无败事).
story.zh: 《老子》第六十四章：“民之从事，常于几成而败之。慎终如始，则无败事。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前5—前3世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 5th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: Advice or praise for sustained care; formal. Related to 善始善终 but stresses caution at the end.
usage.zh: 用于告诫或称赞始终谨慎；较正式。与“善始善终”相近，但强调结尾的谨慎。

natural: a beauty at life's dusk

meaning.en: A beautiful woman growing old; also a lament for talented people who age without achieving their ambitions.
meaning.zh: 美貌的女子渐渐衰老；也比喻有才之士年华老去而抱负未展的感慨。

equivalents: a lament for the passing of one's prime

examples.zh: 看着镜中的自己，她不由感叹美人迟暮。
examples.en: Looking in the mirror she sighed over a beauty's fading.

examples.zh: 英雄末路，美人迟暮，读来令人唏嘘。
examples.en: Heroes at their end and beauties at their dusk: it makes you sigh.

examples.zh: 这位老将军壮志未酬，读到“美人迟暮”不禁黯然。
examples.en: Unfulfilled in his ambitions, the old general felt gloomy on reading 'beauty at dusk'.

story.en: In Li Sao, Qu Yuan laments: 'I fear the grasses and trees will wither, and that the fair one will be late, at dusk of life' (惟草木之零落兮，恐美人之迟暮).
story.zh: 屈原《离骚》：“日月忽其不淹兮，春与秋其代序。惟草木之零落兮，恐美人之迟暮。”

date.en: Warring States, c. early 3rd c. BC

usage.en: Literary lament; the original 美人 referred to an ideal ruler or oneself, later read as a woman growing old.
usage.zh: 书面感叹；《离骚》原意“美人”指理想的君主或诗人自己，后多指女子衰老。

natural: go slowly and it comes out well

meaning.en: Take things slowly and carefully, and they will turn out well; haste spoils them.
meaning.zh: 遇事不要急躁，缓一缓、慢慢处理，反而能圆满解决。

equivalents: no need to rush; it will work out

examples.zh: 别着急答复，事缓则圆。
examples.en: Don't rush your reply; slow handling gets a better result.

examples.zh: 谈判卡住了，不妨先放一放，事缓则圆。
examples.en: The talks are stuck, so let it rest; patience resolves things.

examples.zh: 事缓则圆，这件事不用逼得太紧。
examples.en: Things resolve when taken slowly; there's no need to push too hard on this.

usage.en: Advice for conflicts and negotiations; the opposite of acting on impulse. Often with 事急则乱.
usage.zh: 常用于劝人处理矛盾、谈判时不要急躁，常与“事急则乱”对举。

natural: difficult in the extreme

meaning.en: Extremely difficult; hard even by the standards of hard things.
meaning.zh: 形容非常困难，难到极点。

examples.zh: 要在一周内学会这门语言，真是难乎其难。
examples.en: To learn this language in a week is difficult in the extreme.

examples.zh: 让两家公司合并，谈何容易，简直难乎其难。
examples.en: Merging the two firms is far from easy; it is hard in the extreme.

examples.zh: 在这样的环境里保持清廉，难乎其难。
examples.en: Staying clean in such an environment is exceedingly hard.

usage.en: Predicate; slightly formal, an emphatic form of 难.
usage.zh: 作谓语，略带书面色彩，是“难”的强调说法。

natural: mountains high and rivers far

meaning.en: High mountains and distant rivers; a long and difficult journey, or great distance between people.
meaning.zh: 山又高，水又远；形容路途遥远艰难，也指相隔遥远。

equivalents: a long way off over hill and dale

examples.zh: 山高水远，探亲一趟不容易。
examples.en: With such a long journey over mountains and rivers, visiting relatives is no easy matter.

examples.zh: 山高水远，我们很难常见面。
examples.en: With such distance between us we can seldom meet.

examples.zh: 他不怕山高水远，坚持到边疆支教。
examples.en: Undaunted by the distance, he insisted on teaching in the frontier region.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; neutral-to-sad about distance. 山长水远 is an equal alternative form.
usage.zh: 作谓语、定语，描述路远，略带感伤。“山长水远”是同义的另一说法。

natural: strange look, strange shape

meaning.en: Looking odd or ridiculous in appearance or manner.
meaning.zh: 形容样子、装扮奇怪，不伦不类。

examples.zh: 他穿得怪模怪样，引得路人回头看。
examples.en: He was dressed so oddly that passers-by turned to look.

examples.zh: 这只玩具做得怪模怪样，孩子却很喜欢。
examples.en: The toy looks weird, yet the child loves it.

examples.zh: 别学那些怪模怪样的做派。
examples.en: Don't imitate those ridiculous mannerisms.

usage.en: Colloquial; 模 here is mú (shape, look). Often critical or teasing.
usage.zh: 口语，“模”读 mú（样子）。多含批评或戏谑。

literal: can · pinch (finger-count) · know how to · calculate
natural: good at counting off on the fingers

meaning.en: Good at figuring things out quickly, as if able to count them off on one's fingers; also, a knack for predicting.
meaning.zh: 善于盘算、推算，仿佛掐指一算就知道；也指善于预测。

examples.zh: 他能掐会算，一看就知道今年收成如何。
examples.en: He can work things out in a flash and tell at a glance how this year's harvest will be.

examples.zh: 管账的老伙计能掐会算，从不出错。
examples.en: The old bookkeeper is a whiz at figures and never errs.

examples.zh: 别以为你能掐会算，市场变化谁也说不准。
examples.en: Don't think you can predict everything; no one can be sure how markets move.

usage.en: Colloquial; may mean mental arithmetic, shrewd planning or fortune-telling; often teasing.
usage.zh: 口语，可指心算、精打细算或掐指预测，常带戏谑。
